A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OOPE/OOPE-FW research. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison. The proof appendices are retained; v1's experimental Appendix C is replaced by v3's Section 6.

before.justification: Appendix C, Figures 1–2 report original synthetic linear-bandit simulations measuring regret under different offline-data quantities and coverage.

after.justification: Section 6, Figures 1–4 report original simulations comparing OOPE with online phased elimination, warm-started LinUCB/LinTS and OOPE-FW.

M1.justification: The principal OOPE and OOPE-FW procedures remain unchanged. V3 adds a horizon-free adaptation using increasing horizons, full restarts and recomputed offline weights/effective dimensions (Remark 4.7), plus optional preliminary exploration to satisfy the offline-sample condition (Section 3).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic spherical linear bandits with Gaussian reward noise. V1 explicitly includes rank-deficient offline coverage: five supported arms in ten dimensions. V3's reported experiments use larger, full-dimensional random supports and do not retain that explicit missing-directions scenario. No new application domain or external dataset is introduced.

E2.justification: V1's empirical figures contain only OOPE under different offline-data quantities. V3 adds online phased elimination (Figure 1), warm-started LinUCB and LinTS (Figure 2), and direct OOPE-versus-OOPE-FW comparisons (Figures 3–4). The warm-started methods were previously discussed theoretically but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: V1 evaluates a modification that reuses all offline and previous online data with phase-dependent weighting; v3 states it implements Section 4's prescribed OOPE. Dimensions, arm counts, horizons and offline allocation procedures also change. New experiments include fixed-spectrum effective-dimension sweeps across multiple horizons and dimensions (Tables 2–5).

E4.justification: Beyond v1's offline-data quantity and coverage studies, v3 investigates whether Frank-Wolfe improves OOPE and how that comparison depends on effective dimension, horizon and ambient dimension (Figures 3–4). This adds substantial sensitivity analysis of the approximation's benefits and failure regimes.

E5.justification: V1 displays variability through boxplots without specifying repeat counts. V3 explicitly reports 50 runs per horizon and mean-regret confidence intervals; Figure 1 specifies 95% intervals. This changes statistical reporting but does not establish an increase over v1's unstated run count.

E6.justification: The original boxplot results are replaced by new results under different settings. Figure 2 shows OOPE outperforming LinTS and outperforming LinUCB at longer, but not the shortest, horizons. Figures 3–4 add FW gains and performance reversals across regimes. These are new findings, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V3 adds a horizon-free regret argument and a quantified additional-regret bound for preliminary exploration. The effective-dimension definition, principal upper/lower bounds and Appendix A/B proofs remain substantively unchanged. New Table 1 summarizes existing bounds rather than introducing new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same OOPE, spectral lower-bound and FW claims. V3 newly asserts that the fixed-design setting was previously unstudied (Section 3). Its conclusion also explicitly qualifies minimax matching by the well-/poorly-explored regimes and additive constants, qualifications already present elsewhere in v1.

C2.justification: V3 pinpoints the unresolved intermediate-regime bound gap to a uniform eigenvalue bound (Remark 4.12), extending v1's general confidence-width explanation. It interprets the new FW experiments through approximation costs, sparse-support savings and insufficient exploitation time at short horizons. The fixed-design and no-drift restrictions remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds explicit parameter tables, a random-partition recipe for offline allocations, and initialization details for warm-started LinUCB and LinTS. These improve experimental documentation. The PDFs still provide no code-access instructions or numerical solver specifications.

R1.justification: V3 adds Besson and Kaufmann (2018) for the doubling-trick extension and newly positions the fixed-design setting as previously unstudied. The related-work survey and other cited works are essentially retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and proof structure is retained. V3 separates stationarity and fixed-design assumptions, adds focused explanations, rewrites the conclusion and moves the expanded experiments into Section 6. Author information and publication headers are also updated.

P2.justification: The two appendix boxplot figures are replaced by four main-text figures featuring regret curves, comparator legends, confidence intervals and a three-panel sensitivity analysis. V3 also adds bounds-summary Table 1 and experimental-parameter Tables 2–5, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens empirical validation: v1 tests a data-reusing modification without algorithm baselines, whereas v3 reports the prescribed OOPE procedure, relevant comparisons, repeated-run uncertainty and both favorable and unfavorable FW regimes. This addresses important gaps between the theoretical contributions and their empirical support while retaining the proofs. These gains outweigh losing the explicit rank-deficient experiment, although evaluation remains synthetic and Figure 2 does not support uniform superiority at every horizon.
